about.title: Calistoga Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Calistoga draws visitors year-round to its spas, wineries, and small-town shops along Lincoln Avenue, but uneven walkways, wet pool decks, and poorly lit parking areas can turn a pleasant visit into an injury. Under California law, a property owner or business isn't automatically responsible just because someone got hurt on their premises — you generally need to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazardous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why acting quickly matters: photos of the hazard, incident reports, and surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten within days. Our team evaluates what happened, gathers the right evidence, and explains your options. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and we handle premises liability cases on contingency — meaning no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Video and Evidence Fade Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a store, hotel, or winery is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting early gives us a chance to send a preservation request before that evidence is gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule can still allow a recovery reduced by your share of fault, rather than blocking it outright.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Calistoga?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I fell at a winery or event venue in Calistoga and I'm not sure who owns the property?
items.answer: That's common in a small town where venues sometimes lease space or use outside vendors for events. We can help sort out ownership and management structure through public records and lease agreements before determining who may be responsible.

items.question: Do I need photos or a report from the time of the fall?
items.answer: Yes, if at all possible — photos of the specific hazard, your shoes, and the surrounding area help show the condition at the time of the incident. If you didn't get photos, we can still work with witness statements, medical records, and any available surveillance video.

items.question: Is there a cost to contact you?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we handle premises liability cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
